task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 11 Commerce Physical education, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 2 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.

modules.title: Physical fitness, wellness and lifestyle
modules.outcome: design a personal fitness plan and track it
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Physical fitness, wellness and lifestyle', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: design a personal fitness plan and track it. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Place it: find where and when 'Physical fitness, wellness and lifestyle' happens, on a map, a timeline or in a local example.
Gather: read or listen to two short sources and note who is speaking and why.
Use it: design a personal fitness plan and track it. Give a reason and one piece of evidence for every point.
Weigh it: say what another person might think, and why, before you decide.
modules.example: Solved: Fitness check: resting pulse, one-minute step test, record, repeat after 4 weeks. FITT: frequency, intensity, time, type. Method: Model run for 'Physical fitness, wellness and lifestyle'. Question: what happened, or what is the situation, and why? Sources: two short extracts, a map or table. Notes: who, what, where, when, why. Answer: three sentences, each with a reason and a piece of evidence. Check: is there a point of view that you have not considered? What a good answer looks like: facts are correct, reasons are linked to evidence, and one other point of view is named fairly.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Design a personal fitness plan and track it: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Fitness has components: cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength, flexibility and body composition. For a 16-year-old at 60 kg and 1.65 m, BMI is 60 / (1.65 x 1.65) = 60 / 2.7225 = 22.0, within the 18.5 to 24.9 normal range.

Step 2, Set heart rate zones. Estimated maximum is 220 - 16 = 204 beats per minute. Moderate to vigorous training of 60 to 85 percent gives about 122 to 173 beats per minute. Count your pulse for 15 seconds after a run and multiply by 4.

Step 3, Apply the FITT idea. Frequency: 5 days a week. Intensity: 70 percent of maximum. Time: 30 to 45 minutes. Type: running, cycling and body-weight exercises. Young people are advised to get at least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity daily.

Step 4, Draw a weekly plan. Mon: 30 min jog. Tue: strength circuit with squats and push-ups. Wed: rest or stretching. Thu: interval run. Fri: swim or cycle. Sat: team game. Sun: walk. Add 8 to 10 hours of sleep and regular water.

Step 5, Track progress. Week 1 test: 1.6 km run in 11 minutes and 15 push-ups. After 8 weeks, record again: 9 minutes 30 seconds and 25 push-ups. That is 1.5 minutes faster and 10 more push-ups. Write what you changed and what helped.
Step 6, Your turn: a student of age 17 wants a heart-rate range of 60 to 85 percent. Model answer: 'Maximum is 203. Range is 0.60 x 203 = 122 to 0.85 x 203 = 173 beats per minute.'

modules.standard: Describe the history and values of the Olympic movement: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.
steps: Step 1, Start in ancient Greece. The ancient games were held at Olympia, traditionally dated from 776 BCE, every four years in honour of Zeus. A truce let athletes travel safely. They were ended around 393 CE.

Step 2, Move to the revival. Pierre de Coubertin helped found the International Olympic Committee on 23 June 1894. The first modern Games were held in Athens in 1896 with 14 nations. Women first competed in 1900 in Paris.

Step 3, Calculate the numbering. Paris hosted in 2024. (2024 - 1896) / 4 = 32, so it was the 33rd Olympiad counting 1896 as the first. Games were cancelled in 1916, 1940 and 1944 because of the world wars, but the count continues.

Step 4, Learn symbols and values. The five rings stand for the continents joined together, and the motto is Citius, Altius, Fortius: faster, higher, stronger. Olympic values are excellence, friendship and respect. Winter Games began at Chamonix in 1924.

Step 5, Link to society. The Paralympic Games began as an official event in Rome in 1960 and now run alongside the Olympics. Write a model answer: 'Sport can unite people across nations and promote fair play, while hosting costs and doping show the challenges.'
Step 6, Your turn: what does 'respect' mean in Olympic values? Model answer: 'It means treating opponents, officials and rules fairly, such as shaking hands after a match whether you win or lose.'
